problem_statement: TCP input retention preserves the wrong bytes: a callback retaining a suffix receives an old prefix on the next delivery. Preserve the requested trailing bytes in order across deliveries.
synthetic_mechanism: Compaction copies from the buffer start rather than the retained suffix. Retention lengths, bounds checks, and registration initialization remain correct.
validation_scope: Native component tests of real upstream production source; not full RTOS, radio, or hardware validation.
original_problem: TCP socket input callbacks can request that an unconsumed suffix remain buffered, but those bytes are lost or overwritten when more data arrives. Retained bytes must be presented in order together with subsequent data, including when a single incoming segment exceeds the input buffer size. A newly registered socket must start with no retained data. Requests to retain more bytes than were delivered must stay bounded, and receiving more data while the buffer is entirely retained must return without overwriting it or looping indefinitely. Preserve ordinary reception, binary payloads, callbacks that consume all data, sockets without input callbacks, and send-queue behavior.
